Facing the Paperwork You Keep Avoiding

For the form, claim or renewal that has been on the kitchen table for a month and grows heavier every time you walk past. It helps you find out what it actually needs, do one piece of it today, and stop the deadline from arriving first.

Stress · Stress · Habits · 8 items · whenever you need it

The checklist

  • Read it once and write the deadline down — most of the dread is not knowing the date.
  • List what you need to gather, not what to do — admin stalls on missing documents.
  • Find the hardest document first — the rest is usually fifteen minutes after that.
  • Fill in only the boxes you can answer now — a half-done form is further along than a blank one.
  • Call the number on it with your question — the people on that line do this all day.
  • Book twenty minutes for it in the calendar — avoided tasks need a slot, not more resolve.
  • Do it at a table, not on your phone — the wrong setup is half the reason it stalls.
  • Put it in the mail or hit send the same day — a finished form on the table is still unfinished.

Use this checklist Free account: tick items off and keep each day's record.

How to use it

Run through it whenever you need it, honestly and without scoring yourself. A checklist is a way of noticing, not a test: an item you cannot tick is information about the day, not a verdict on you. Over a few weeks the pattern of what gets ticked and what does not says more than any single pass.

With a free Theraglee account the checklist remembers each pass, so you can look back. Without one, you can still read it here and keep your own copy.
